steps.title: Euthanize mice
steps.instruction: Euthanize C57BL/6J mice on day 8 of oral DSS treatment or on day 2 of intrarectal TNBS instillation.

steps.title: Dissect intestine and keep cold
steps.instruction: Spray the mouse abdomen with 70 % industrial methylated spirit (IMS), dissect out the small or large intestine, quickly remove surrounding connective tissue, and place the intestinal tissue in 2 mL ice‑cold cRPMI in a 6‑well plate (lid on). Transfer the plate to a biosafety cabinet (Category 2) in the tissue‑culture room.

steps.title: Epithelial removal incubation
steps.instruction: Open the intestine longitudinally, wash out feces with room‑temperature (RT) washing solution, blot excess liquid with paper, cut the tissue into ~1 cm pieces, and immerse the pieces in pre‑warmed epithelial removal solution (30 mL per colon) in a conical tube. Incubate horizontally on a shaker at 37 °C, 200 rpm for 10 min (optimize: 15 min for untreated ileum, 5–10 min for inflamed colon).

steps.title: Wash tissues post‑epithelial removal
steps.instruction: Wash the tissues with 30 mL RT washing solution to remove EDTA, then collect the tissue in a sterile Petri dish for the next step.

steps.title: Enzymatic digestion of tissue
steps.instruction: On a sterile plastic Petri dish, mince the intestinal tissue into smaller pieces with a sterile scalpel. Transfer the minced tissue to a 50 mL tube and add 5 mL freshly prepared digestion solution (pre‑warmed at 37 °C, prepared within 30 min). Incubate the tube vertically in a 37 °C incubator without shaking for 10 min. For Peyer’s patches, place 1–2 mL digestion solution directly on the patches without mincing. Use Medicon MAX (16 mL capacity) for lamina propria, Medicon 1.6 mL for Peyer’s patches or small organs; MLNs require no digestion and are placed directly into Medicons.

steps.title: Mechanical dissociation and collection
steps.instruction: Vortex the digestion tubes at maximum speed for 5–10 s, then collect the supernatant (containing single cells) through a 100 µm cell strainer into a fresh 50 mL tube. Transfer the remaining tissue on the strainer into a Medicon MAX using sterile tweezers, add 15–16 mL cold cRPMI (8–10 °C) through the Medicon’s collecting port with a syringe, and place the Medicon MAX into the Medimachine II. Dissociate for 10 s at medium speed (≈10 000 rpm). Collect the liquid with a sterile syringe, combine it with the earlier supernatant, filter again through a 100 µm strainer, and add cold cRPMI to a final volume of 45 mL. Keep the tube on ice. (For Peyer’s patches: skip vortex, add 1.6 mL cold cRPMI, then dissociate as above. For MLNs: place directly into Medicons, collect cells through a 70 µm strainer into 15 mL tubes and add cRPMI to a final 10 mL.)

steps.title: Centrifugation and RBC lysis (if needed)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the cell suspension at 450 × g for 15 min at 10 °C. Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 35 mL cold cRPMI (8–10 °C), then filter through a 40 µm cell strainer into a new tube. If the pellet appears reddish (indicative of red blood cells), perform RBC lysis: gently resuspend the pellet in 500 µL ice‑cold RBC lysis buffer, incubate 3–4 min at RT, add 10 mL cold cRPMI, centrifuge again at 450 × g for 15 min at 10 °C, wash once with 10 mL cold cRPMI, and keep on ice.

steps.title: Final resuspension
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube again at 450 × g for 15 min at 10 °C, discard the supernatant, and resuspend the cell pellet in the desired volume of cold cRPMI (e.g., 2 mL for colonic or ileal lamina propria, 1 mL for Peyer’s patches or MLNs).

steps.title: Viability assessment and flow cytometry staining
steps.instruction: Assess cell viability with Trypan Blue exclusion (mix cell suspension and Trypan Blue 1:1, load onto a hemocytometer, count under a light microscope). Then stain cells for flow cytometry as follows:

substeps.instruction: a. Resuspend 1 × 10⁶ cells in 100 µL 10 mM HEPES buffer containing the chosen live/dead fixable viability dye (e.g., ViaKrome 808 or eFluor 780) at the manufacturer‑recommended concentration. Incubate 15 min in the refrigerator, wash with 10 mM HEPES, and centrifuge at 450 × g for 6 min at 10 °C.

b. Prepare a 1:100 dilution of Fc‑blocking solution (anti‑mouse CD16/CD32) in FACS buffer; add 10 µL per tube and incubate 5 min at RT. Add surface antibodies at the indicated dilutions (CD45 1:100, Ly6G 1:50, CD11b 1:100), bring the volume to 100 µL with FACS buffer, and incubate 20 min in the dark at 4 °C. Wash twice with FACS buffer, centrifuging each time at 450 × g for 6 min at 10 °C.
c. For fixation, mix intracellular fixation buffer with FACS buffer 1:1, resuspend the cell pellet in 100 µL of this diluted fixation solution, and store in the dark at 4 °C until analysis.
